paginate_cols(at = 1) stops: "`at` must name columns 2..ncol -- there is nothing before column 1."; a column that is not there stops: "`paginate_cols(at)` index 9 out of range (1..5)."; cols that is not a list stops: "`cols` must be a list of column blocks (names or positions)."; a by that is neither a separator found in the names nor one key per column stops: "`by` must be a single separator found in the column names, or one key per column (<n>)."

paginate_cols() with every column a kept column stops: "`paginate_cols()` produced no column blocks: every column is a carry (row-heading) column."; a by that leaves none, "`by` left no columns to split: every column is a carry column."

paginate_cols() given a list that is not rtftable pages stops: "`paginate_cols()` on a list expects every element to be an rtftable (as returned by as_rtftables()); element 1 is '<class>'."; pages with differing columns stop: "`paginate_cols()` needs every page to have the same columns; page 1 has <n> and page 2 has <m>."

paginate_cols(fit = ) that is not TRUE or FALSE stops: "`paginate_cols(fit = )` is TRUE (page 1's scale on every block) or FALSE (each column keeps its width)."; a width or page_order outside its values stops (match.arg(), or "`page_order`: \"x\" is not an axis. Give the axes outermost first, from ..." / "`page_order`: each axis may appear once.").
notes: no test of the fit stop() text found

statement: paginate_cols(col_header = "names") without a by that is one separator stops: "`col_header = \"names\"` needs `by` to be the separator in the column names (e.g. by = \"____\")."; a label-row col_header of the wrong width stops: "`paginate_cols(col_header)`: the label row has <n> labels but the table has <m> printed columns. ..."

paginate_cols(allow_span_break = FALSE) with a cut inside a spanning header cell stops: "`paginate_cols()` would break the spanning header cell '<label>' (columns <a>..<b>) at column <c>. Move the cut to a group boundary, or pass allow_span_break = TRUE."
paginate_cols(positon = ) (an argument it does not have) warns and ignores it: "`paginate_cols()`: unknown argument `positon` ... ignored. Valid arguments: ..."
as_rtftables(cell_format = , align_count_pct = ): a cell_format given takes precedence and align_count_pct is ignored.

as_rtftables(col_header = ) in ..., an explicit value, wins over the header rebuilt from delimited names (header_sep), over the header a source or a listing spec supplies, and over the labels read from the source.

as_rtftables(listing = ) supplies defaults only: group_col, group_by, split (group_safe when max_rows is set), drop_cols, blank_row_first, col_header, col_rel_width and collapse_repeats are never overridden by the listing when the caller passed them.

as_rtftables(table_width_twips = , table_width_pct = , col_rel_width = , column_widths_twips = , auto_width = ): column_widths_twips wins outright and its sum is the table's width, col_rel_width apportions whatever the total is, table_width_twips wins over table_width_pct, and with none of them the writable page width is used; an explicit col_rel_width also wins over auto_width.

as_rtftables(stub = , split = "by_value"): the body is split by group_col first and the stub is built on each page afterwards, so group_col means the pre-stub columns and is not folded into the stub; with any other split the stub is built first and group_col, drop_cols, sort_by and group_by = "indent" mean the reshaped columns.

as_rtftables(page_by = ) changes the meaning of group_col and split: group_col left NULL becomes the first column not named in page_by, and with split = "by_value" the group is the outer axis and page_by the inner one, a group's pages keeping its name alone.

as_rtftables(drop_cols = ) changes the coordinates other arguments are written in: col_header (and paginate_cols positions) are resolved against the final printed columns, while col_spec, col_rel_width and row_title use the pre-drop input coordinates and are reindexed to the kept columns.

as_rtftables(sort_by = ) is applied first, so group detection, the continuation labels and blank_rows positions all see the sorted order, and cell_styles follow their rows; a sort key may be listed in drop_cols to order on a column that is not printed.

as_rtftables(count_blank_rows = TRUE, blank_rows = "between_groups" / blank_rows_by_change()): a separator blank never lands on a page's first or last row, a separator survives where a page holds two groups, and an explicit position is honoured wherever it lands.

set_col_header() after paginate_cols(): a header written for the whole table does not fit pages that kept only some of its columns and is refused; it is set before the split (then sliced per page, spanning cells clipped), or passed as paginate_cols(col_header = ).

paginate_cols(order = ) changes where rtf_tables(auto_section = TRUE) opens sections: a section opens where the page name changes, so "down" keeps a table's column pages in one section, while "across" interleaves the names and gives a section per page.

set_blank_rows() resolves a blank_rows specification (positions, "between_groups", or blank_rows_by_change() / blank_rows_by_rule() specs) into integer positions and stores them on attr(data, "rtf_blank_rows") of one page-sized data frame; as_rtftables() calls it on every page.
blank_rows_by_change() builds a blank-row spec that inserts a blank separator row each time the group of any listed column changes from the previous row.
blank_rows_by_rule() builds a blank-row spec that inserts a blank separator row before or after every data row whose value in one column matches a regular expression.

set_decimal_split() marks body columns of an rtftable (or of every page of a list) to be written as two adjacent RTF cells, the part before the decimal separator right-aligned and the separator with everything after it left-aligned, so the decimal points line up; it is an output option and never rewrites the data.
auto_col_widths() estimates a width in twips for each column of a data frame from its header label and values, for rtftable(column_widths_twips = ).

default_col_widths() returns the relative column widths rtftable() uses when a table gives no widths: row-heading columns as wide as their longest line within a share of the table, the data columns sharing the rest, and a data column whose longest cell does not fit widened from the others.
text_width_in() estimates the display width, in inches, of character strings in a given font and size.
style_body() restyles chosen body cells of a finished rtftable (or of every page of a list): bold, italic, underline, indent, colour, background, alignment and border, per row and column selection.
style_cols() restyles whole columns of a finished rtftable (or of every page of a list): body alignment, bold, italic, underline, indent, colour, fill, border, and the header-label look.
style_header() restyles the column-header rows of a finished rtftable (or of every page of a list): label, border, alignment, bold, italic and underline on the targeted header cells.
style_zone() merges rtf_border() overrides, side by side, into the zones (header, spanning, body, first_row, last_row) of a finished rtftable's border (or of every page of a list).

rtf_table_style() bundles table-wide formatting defaults (zone borders, alignment, bold, italic, underline, cell padding, row height) into one immutable record passed as rtftable(style = ) or as_rtftables(style = ).
rtf_table_style_tfl() returns a freshly built rtf_table_style holding the clinical TFL preset: rules on the column-header block only, no vertical lines, no bold headers, no borders on the data.
rtf_table_style_with() returns a copy of an rtf_table_style with the named fields replaced, leaving the original unchanged.
rtf_table_border() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) builds the per-zone border map of a table from rtf_border() objects, with whole-table outer, inside_h and inside_v shortcuts.

rtf_border() builds a border for a selection (a cell, a row kind, the whole table) from its four outer edges and the rules inside it, each side TRUE / FALSE, a style name, an rtf_border_line() or NULL.
rtf_border_bottom() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) builds a border with a bottom edge only; it is rtf_border(bottom = TRUE).
rtf_border_box() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) builds a border with all four outer edges alike; it is rtf_border(all = TRUE).
rtf_border_line() builds the line of one border side: its style, weight in twips and colour, with style "none" as an explicit no-line.
rtf_border_none() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) builds a border with no side set; it is rtf_border().
rtf_border_side() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) is the old name of rtf_border_line().
rtf_border_tfl() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) returns the clinical TFL per-zone border: a top and a bottom rule on the column-header block only.
rtf_border_top() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) builds a border with a top edge only; it is rtf_border(top = TRUE).
rtf_border_with() (deprecated in 0.8.x, removed in 0.9.0) returns a copy of an rtf_border with the named sides replaced.
cell_rows() builds a cells recipe of several named rows, each row's value being a template, a chain of templates or a chain with guards, for widen_ard(cells = ) and plan_cells().
col_cell() builds one cell of a column-header row: the columns it covers (by position, name, range or selector function), its label, alignment, bold / italic / underline and its own border.
col_key() builds a column selector for col_cell(pos = ) that keeps the columns whose name segment (split on a separator) is one of the given keys.

set_blank_rows(data, ...) returns data with the resolved positions as attr(data, "rtf_blank_rows"): sorted, unique integers, 0 meaning a blank row before the first row and k a blank row after row k; the data itself is not changed.
set_blank_rows(data = ) takes a data frame or tibble and returns it with the same class (a tibble stays a tibble).
set_blank_rows() on anything that is not a data frame stops: "`data` must be a data.frame (or tibble)."
set_blank_rows(blank_rows = NULL) (the default) adds no positions of its own; with blank_row_first and blank_row_end also FALSE the attribute is left absent (NULL), not an empty vector.
set_blank_rows(blank_rows = <integer vector>) takes explicit positions, 0 before the first row and k after row k.

set_blank_rows(blank_rows = <integer vector>) drops, without a warning, a position that is NA, below 0 (so -1, which rtftable(blank_rows = ) reads as after the last row, is dropped) or above nrow(data).
notes: help does not say that out-of-range and negative positions are silently dropped here, while rtftable(blank_rows = ) warns for them

statement: set_blank_rows(blank_rows = "between_groups") puts a blank row after the last row of every group, at each transition between groups found by group_col and group_by, never before the first or after the last row.
set_blank_rows(blank_rows = ) takes a blank_rows_by_change() or blank_rows_by_rule() spec and resolves it on this data frame, so each page of as_rtftables() is resolved on its own rows.
set_blank_rows(blank_rows = list(...)) combines any of the forms in one plain list: the positions of every entry are unioned and duplicates dropped.
set_blank_rows(blank_rows = ) with an entry that is none of those (a string other than "between_groups", say) stops: "Unrecognised `blank_rows` entry: <entry>".
set_blank_rows(blank_row_first = TRUE) also adds position 0, a blank row at the top of data; the default is FALSE.
set_blank_rows(blank_row_end = TRUE) also adds position nrow(data), a blank row at the bottom of data; the default is FALSE.

set_blank_rows(group_col = ) names the column (by name or 1-based position) on which "between_groups" detects groups; NULL (the default) detects on column 1; it is used only with blank_rows = "between_groups".
set_blank_rows(group_col = ) naming no column stops: "`group_col` 'nope' not found in the table."; a position outside the data stops: "`group_col` index 9 out of range (1..2)."

set_blank_rows(group_by = ) is "auto" by default, or "indent", "value" or "filled": how groups are recognised for blank_rows = "between_groups", the same detection as the pagination splits; any other value is refused by match.arg().
set_blank_rows(df = ) is the old name of data: it still works and warns once a session, "`set_blank_rows(df = )` is deprecated: the argument is `data` now.  The old name is removed in 0.9.0."

blank_rows_by_change() returns an object of class rtf_blank_rows_by_change holding cols, group_by, include_before_first and include_after_last; it inserts nothing itself, the table that receives it (rtftable(blank_rows = ), as_rtftables(blank_rows = ), set_blank_rows(blank_rows = )) does.
blank_rows_by_change(cols = ) names the columns to watch; a blank row falls after each row that is followed by a row of another group, in any of them.
blank_rows_by_change(cols = ) that is not a character vector or is empty stops: "`cols` must be a non-empty character vector."
blank_rows_by_change(group_by = "value") (the default) makes a group a run of equal values, so a blank falls wherever a value differs from the previous row.

blank_rows_by_change(group_by = "indent") makes a non-indented, non-empty cell start a group, indented and empty cells being members; the blanks fall where blank_rows = "between_groups" with the same group_by puts them.
blank_rows_by_change(group_by = "filled") makes a non-empty cell start a group, NA and "" cells being members.
blank_rows_by_change(group_by = "auto") picks "value", "indent" or "filled" from each column's content.
blank_rows_by_change(group_by = ) outside "value", "indent", "filled", "auto" is refused by match.arg() ("'arg' should be one of ...").
blank_rows_by_change(include_before_first = TRUE) (the default) also puts a blank row before the first data row; FALSE leaves it out. Any value other than TRUE counts as FALSE.
blank_rows_by_change(include_after_last = TRUE) (the default) also puts a blank row after the last data row; FALSE leaves it out. Any value other than TRUE counts as FALSE.
blank_rows_by_change() with a column that is not in the data warns "blank_rows_by_change column 'x' not found; ignored." and still applies the other columns.
blank_rows_by_change() on a data frame with no rows gives no blank row at all; on one row there is no change to find, so only the before-first and after-last rows are added.

A blank_rows_by_change() spec resolved on a page (as_rtftables(), set_blank_rows()) acts as a separator and never falls on the page's first or last row, whatever include_before_first and include_after_last say.
blank_rows_by_rule() returns an object of class rtf_blank_rows_by_rule holding col, pattern and where; the table that receives it inserts the rows.
blank_rows_by_rule(col = ) names the one column whose values are tested.
blank_rows_by_rule(col = ) that is not one character string stops: "`col` must be a single column name."
blank_rows_by_rule(pattern = ) is a regular expression matched with grepl() against the column as character; a row matches when the pattern is found in its value, an NA value never matches.
blank_rows_by_rule(pattern = ) that is not one character string stops: "`pattern` must be a single regular expression."
blank_rows_by_rule(where = "before") (the default) puts a blank row before every matching row, so a match on row k gives position k - 1 and a match on the first row gives 0.
blank_rows_by_rule(where = "after") puts a blank row after every matching row, position k for a match on row k.
blank_rows_by_rule(where = ) other than "before" or "after" is refused by match.arg().
blank_rows_by_rule() with a column that is not in the data warns "blank_rows_by_rule column 'x' not found; ignored." and adds no blank row.
blank_rows_by_rule() whose pattern matches no row, or applied to a data frame with no rows, adds no blank row.
A blank_rows_by_rule() spec resolved on a page (as_rtftables(), set_blank_rows()) acts as a separator and never falls on the page's first or last row.

set_decimal_split(x, cols = ) stores the split on the table as x$decimal_split and changes only the RTF output: the data frame is never rewritten, the console preview does not show the split, and a table without the option renders byte for byte as before.
set_decimal_split(x = ) takes an rtftable, or a list of rtftable pages as as_rtftables() returns, and applies the setting to every page of the list.

set_decimal_split() on a list holding something that is not an rtftable stops: "`set_decimal_split()` on a list expects every element to be an rtftable (as returned by as_rtftables()); element 1 is 'numeric'."
set_decimal_split(cols = ) names the columns to split, by name or position (mix them in a list()), resolved against the table's final printed columns and stored as positions.
set_decimal_split(cols = NULL), given explicitly, clears a previously set split.
set_decimal_split() called without cols stops: "`set_decimal_split()`: `cols` is required. To clear a previously set split, pass `cols = NULL` explicitly."
notes: help for cols says only that NULL clears the setting; it does not say that leaving cols out is an error

statement: set_decimal_split(cols = ) naming a column the table does not have stops: "`set_decimal_split(cols)` column 'Nope' not found in the table."; a position outside the table stops: "`set_decimal_split(cols)` index 9 out of range (1..n)."

set_decimal_split() with an argument it does not have (a misspelt cols = colS, say) warns once per call, "`set_decimal_split()`: unknown argument `colS` (did you mean `cols`?) ignored." with the list of valid arguments, instead of silently ignoring it (#301).

set_decimal_split(ratio = NULL) (the default) sizes the two halves from the widest left and right part actually present in the column; a number strictly between 0 and 1 is the left half's share of the column and keeps the split point identical across pages.
set_decimal_split(ratio = ) that is not one number strictly between 0 and 1 stops: "`ratio` must be a single number strictly between 0 and 1."
set_decimal_split(decimal_mark = ".") (the default) is the separator the cells are split at, the first one in the cell; another single string splits there instead.
set_decimal_split(decimal_mark = ) that is not one non-empty string stops: "`decimal_mark` must be a single non-empty string."

set_decimal_split(pad_chars = c(1, 1)) (the default) is the room added to each measured half before the ratio is taken, in character widths, integer half first; c(0, 0) with min_chars c(0, 0) gives the raw measured ratio.
set_decimal_split(min_chars = c(4, 6)) (the default) is the floor for each half after pad_chars, so a short column holds a 4 : 6 baseline and a larger one scales from its own measurement.

set_decimal_split(max_chars = 10) (the default) is the total measured width above which the allowance is dropped and the raw measured proportions are used; the boundary is exclusive (10 keeps the allowance) and Inf never drops it.

set_decimal_split(pad_chars = ) or (min_chars = ) that is not two non-negative numbers stops: "`pad_chars` must be two non-negative numbers (integer half, decimal half)."; max_chars that is not one positive number (or Inf) stops: "`max_chars` must be a single positive number (or Inf)."
set_decimal_split(pad_chars = NULL, min_chars = NULL, max_chars = NULL) mean the documented defaults.
set_decimal_split(include_compound = FALSE) (the default) leaves a compound value such as "12.3 (4.56)" as one cell across the pair; TRUE splits it too.

A cell is split when it starts with an optional prefix (<, >, >=, <=, ~, +, -) followed by a digit or the separator and holds a digit: the prefix goes with the left half and a suffix (%, a footnote marker) with the right half; "100" gives "100" and an empty right half.
Free text such as "n (%)" or a group label is not split and is written as one cell across the pair as without the option; empty and NA cells give two empty halves.
Leading and trailing spaces, non-breaking ones included (as left by fmt_right_align()), are dropped from split cells.
A selected column in which no cell carries the separator is left untouched; this is decided per table, so across paginated pages a column may be split on one page and not on another.

A split column is written as two cells, the integer half right-aligned and the decimal half left-aligned, carrying the split text; the table's total width is unchanged (only the column's own width is divided), and a row whose cell is not split keeps the column's own alignment.
The column header keeps rendering over the original single column: data rows gain a cell, the header and spanning cells keep the original geometry.
A table made of several data frames has every one of them scanned for the separator, and the setting survives paginate_cols().
auto_col_widths(data) returns an integer vector of widths in twips, one per column of data, derived from the longest line of the header label and of the values in the font and size given.
auto_col_widths(data = ) is the data frame to measure (its first argument); df = is the old name, still working and not warned.
auto_col_widths() given neither data nor df, or something that is not a data frame, stops: "`data` must be a data.frame."

auto_col_widths(col_header = ) gives the header labels to measure: NULL (the default) uses names(data); a character vector, a pipe-delimited string, or a list of character vectors (only the first row counted). Missing labels count as empty.

auto_col_widths(font = , font_size_half_points = 18L) set the font (NULL is getOption("rtfreporter.font"), as text_width_in()) and the size in half-points (18 = 9 pt) the widths are measured in; size_half_points = is the old name, still working and not warned.
auto_col_widths(table_width_twips = NULL) (the default) leaves the natural widths; a number scales the widths so that they add up to exactly that many twips, the last column absorbing the rounding.
auto_col_widths(min_col_width_twips = 720L) (the default, 0.5 inch) is the floor of every column's width.
auto_col_widths(col_padding_twips = 288L) (the default, 0.2 inch) is added to every column's measured width for cell padding and spacing.

auto_col_widths(protect_cols = integer(0)) names columns kept at their natural width when table_width_twips makes the table narrower, only the other columns being shrunk; protection is dropped when it would push the others below min_col_width_twips.
notes: help says protect_cols "has no effect when scaling up", but the code keeps the protected columns at their natural width and scales only the other columns up to the target, so the table does not scale evenly

statement: auto_col_widths() measures a multi-line cell or label by its longest line, not the sum of its lines.

default_col_widths(data) returns a named numeric vector, one value per column of data and named as its columns, of relative widths scaled so that the smallest data column is 1; rtftable() uses the same proportions when a table gives no widths, as rtftable(col_rel_width = ) and plan_columns(widths = ) take it.
notes: help says col_rel_width = default_col_widths(data) gives "the same table"; the rounding of digits = 1 can differ by a few twips, and the tests compare with digits = 6

statement: default_col_widths() on anything that is not a data frame stops: "`data` must be a data.frame."
default_col_widths(row_title = ) names the row-heading columns by position or name; NULL (the default) is column 1, as in rtftable().

default_col_widths(row_title = ) naming a column that is not there stops: "`row_title` column(s) not found in data: x"; a position outside 1..ncol stops: "`row_title` indices must be within 1..3."; a value that is neither names nor numbers stops: "`row_title` must be NULL, an integer vector, or column names."

default_col_widths(col_header = ) gives the header's labels (one row, or a list of rows of which only the last is counted); NULL (the default) uses names(data). A header wraps, so it counts by its longest word.
default_col_widths(width_chars = 120) (the default, a landscape letter or A4 page in 9-point monospace) is the table's width in characters; it decides whether a long cell fits its share.
default_col_widths(digits = 1L) (the default) is the number of decimals the proportions are rounded to.

The row-heading columns get their longest line plus 2 characters of padding (with some room beyond that where the table has it), within a share of the table of at most 40%, less with many data columns (down to 20%), and 5 points more when the row-heading cells are indented.

The data columns share the rest of the width equally; a data column whose longest cell (or longest header word) does not fit its share is widened, from the other columns as far as they keep what they need.
default_col_widths() reads every cell as character with NA as empty, and measures a multi-line cell by its longest line.
A table with no data column apart from its row headings (or an empty row_title) gets equal widths, 1 for every column.
A table split into column pages by paginate_cols() keeps each column's default width on every block.

text_width_in(text) returns a numeric vector of estimated widths in inches, the same length as text, proportional to the number of characters (exact for a monospace font, an average-width estimate for Arial).
text_width_in(text = ) is a character vector (anything else is coerced with as.character()); NA counts as "" and has width 0.

text_width_in(font = ) is "Courier New" / "courier_new", "Courier" or "Arial", case, spaces and hyphens not mattering; NULL (the default) is the package's font, getOption("rtfreporter.font"), "Courier New".
text_width_in(font = ) with a name it does not know falls back to Courier New widths, without a warning.

text_width_in(font_size_half_points = 18L) (the default, 9 pt) is the size in half-points, the unit of RTF; a larger size gives a wider result. size_half_points = is the old name, still working and not warned.

text_width_in(font = <a named vector of slots>) measures with its latin font; when it has an east_asian slot, each East Asian wide character (CJK, Hangul, kana, fullwidth forms) counts as two columns.

style_body(x, ...) returns a modified copy of the rtftable (or of every page of the list), writing per-cell overrides into cell_styles for the selected rows and columns; it layers on overrides already there without erasing them.

style_body(rows = NULL) (the default) selects every body row; integer positions; a logical vector over all body rows; a predicate function(data) returning one logical per row; or a one-sided formula evaluated in the body data (rows = ~ label == "Mean").
style_body(rows = ) on a table of several data frames counts rows across all of them, evaluates a predicate or formula on each data frame in turn, and an NA result selects nothing.

style_body(rows = ) outside the table stops: "`style_body(rows = )` positions must be in 1..2."; a logical vector of the wrong length, "`style_body(rows = )` logical vector must have length 2 (the number of body rows); got 3."; a predicate that does not return a logical vector of length nrow(data), "`style_body(rows = )` predicate must return a logical vector of length nrow(data) (3); got integer of length 2."

style_body(rows = ) that is a two-sided formula stops: "`style_body(rows = )` formula must be one-sided (~ expr)."; any other type, "`style_body(rows = )` must be NULL, row positions, a logical vector, a predicate function(data), or a one-sided formula."
style_body(cols = NULL) (the default) selects every column; names and positions are mixed with a list(), resolved against the final printed columns.
style_body(cols = ) naming a column that is not there stops: "`style_body(cols)` column 'x' not found in the table."; a position outside the table, "`style_body(cols)` index 9 out of range (1..n)."
style_body(bold = , italic = , underline = ) set the flag on the selected cells; NULL (the default) leaves it as it is.
style_body(bold = ) (likewise italic, underline) that is not TRUE or FALSE stops: "`style_body(bold = )` must be TRUE or FALSE."
style_body(indent_twips = ) sets the left indent of the selected cells, in twips.
style_body(color = ) sets the text colour of the selected cells, as "#RRGGBB".

style_body(background = ) fills the selected cells with a colour "#RRGGBB", overriding the column's own fill; NULL (the default) leaves cells unfilled; an unknown or empty colour is not drawn, and a colour used is added to the document's colour table.
style_body(align = ) is "left", "center" or "right" for the selected cells, overriding the column's alignment cell by cell.
style_body(align = ) outside "left", "center", "right" stops: "`style_body(align = )` must be \"left\", \"center\", or \"right\"."

style_body(border = ) is an rtf_border() merged, per side, on top of the border the row's zone gives (body crossed with first_row and last_row) on the selected cells only; an "none" side erases a zone rule there.
style_body(border = ) that is not an rtf_border() stops: "`style_body(border = )` must be an rtf_border() object."
style_body() keeps per-cell borders and alignments with their rows and columns when as_rtftables(drop_cols = ) removes columns, and a selection that matches no row returns the table unchanged.
style_body(x = <a list of pages>) styles every page, evaluating a predicate or formula per page; integer or logical rows are refused because page-local row numbers are ambiguous.

style_body() on a page list with integer or logical rows stops: "`style_body()` on a page list cannot take integer/logical `rows` -- page-local row numbers are ambiguous across pages. Use a predicate function or one-sided formula (evaluated per page), or style a single page directly."; a list element that is not an rtftable stops: "`style_body()` on a list expects every element to be an rtftable (as returned by as_rtftables()); element 2 is 'data.frame'."
style_body() with an argument it does not have (rows, bolt = TRUE) warns "`style_body()`: unknown argument `bolt` (did you mean `bold`?) ignored." with the valid arguments, and ignores it.

style_cols(x, cols = ) patches the column specification of the selected columns (all when cols is NULL) and returns a modified copy, for a rtftable or each page of a list; the other columns keep their look.

style_cols(cols = ) selects columns by name or position (mixed with a list()), NULL being all; a name not in the table stops with "`style_cols(cols)` column 'nope' not found in the table.", a position outside it with "`style_cols(cols)` index 9 out of range (1..n)."
style_cols(align = ) is "left", "center" or "right" for the body cells of the columns; (header_align = ) the same for the header label.

style_cols(align = ) or (header_align = ) outside "left", "center", "right" stops: "`style_cols(align = )` must be \"left\", \"center\", or \"right\"." (header_align: "`style_cols(align = )` ..." as well, the message names the verb with align).
notes: the message for a bad header_align names `align`, not `header_align`

statement: style_cols(bold = , italic = , underline = ) set the body-cell flag of the columns; (header_bold = , header_italic = ) the look of the header label.
style_cols(bold = ), (italic = ), (underline = ), (header_bold = ) or (header_italic = ) that is not TRUE or FALSE stops: "`style_cols(bold = )` must be TRUE or FALSE." (naming the argument).
style_cols(indent_twips = ) sets the left indent of the columns' body cells, in twips; (color = ) the body text colour "#RRGGBB".

style_cols(background = ) fills the columns' body cells with "#RRGGBB"; (header_background = ) fills the header cells only, kept apart so a shaded header does not shade the body; NULL (the default) leaves cells unfilled.
style_cols(border = ) is an rtf_border() merged, per side, onto the column's border, which draws on the column's header cell.
style_cols(border = ) that is not an rtf_border() stops: "`style_cols(border = )` must be an rtf_border() object."

style_cols() on a page list with an element that is not an rtftable stops: "`style_cols()` on a list expects every element to be an rtftable (as returned by as_rtftables()); element 2 is 'data.frame'."; an argument it does not have warns "`style_cols()`: unknown argument `alignn` (did you mean `align`?) ignored."

style_header(x, ...) returns a modified copy of the rtftable (or of every page of the list), patching the targeted cells of the targeted header rows; a header cell is targeted when its span intersects cols.
style_header(row = NULL) (the default) targets every header row; integer header-row indices, 1 being the top row.
style_header(row = ) outside the header rows stops: "`style_header(row = )` must be in 1..1 (the header rows, top first)."

style_header(cols = ) selects data columns by name or position (mixed with a list()), NULL being all; a spanning cell is targeted when its span intersects cols. A name not in the table stops with "`style_header(cols)` column 'x' not found in the table.", a position outside it with "`style_header(cols)` index 9 out of range (1..n)."
style_header(label = ) replaces the label of the targeted cells on cell rows and on label rows; several labels are recycled over the targeted cells in order.

style_header(border = ) is an rtf_border() merged, per side, onto the targeted cells' border (an existing side survives where the new one is NULL; "none" erases the automatic group underline of a spanning cell); a later call wins per side.
style_header(align = , bold = , italic = , underline = ) set the look of the targeted cells.

style_header() with align outside "left", "center", "right", border that is not an rtf_border(), or a flag that is not TRUE or FALSE stops: "`style_header(align = )` must be \"left\", \"center\", or \"right\"."; "`style_header(border = )` must be an rtf_border() object."; "`style_header(bold = )` must be TRUE or FALSE."

On a character label row, bold, italic and align are stored in the columns' header styling, which every label row of the table shares; with more than one label row style_header() warns "`style_header()`: header text styling (bold/italic/align) is stored per column and shared by ALL label rows."

On a character label row, a border or underline request first promotes the row to an equivalent list of single-column cells (labels and header styling copied over), so the border lands on the requested cell only; the promotion alone does not change the rendered output.
style_header(cols = ) that intersects no cell of a cell row warns "`style_header()`: no header cells intersect the requested columns; nothing changed." and leaves the row as it was.

style_header() on a table with no header of its own makes the columns' names (what is printed) its header and styles that (#749); on a table with no columns it stops "`style_header()`: this rtftable has no column header."
style_header() restyles the header of every data frame of a table made of several, keeping col_header_list in step.

style_header() with an argument it does not have warns "`style_header()`: unknown argument `labl` (did you mean `label`?) ignored." with the valid arguments; a page list holding a non-rtftable stops "`style_header()` on a list expects every element to be an rtftable ...".

style_zone(x, header, spanning, body, first_row, last_row) merges each rtf_border() given, side by side, onto the matching zone of the table's border (a table with no border starts from an empty one) and returns a modified copy; a side left NULL leaves what was there, FALSE or "none" erases it.

style_zone(header = , spanning = , body = , first_row = , last_row = ) are the rtf_border() overrides of the column-header rows, the spanning rows, the data rows, the first data row and the last data row; a zone left NULL is untouched, and a call with none returns the table unchanged.
style_zone() with a zone that is not an rtf_border() stops: "`style_zone(border = )` must be an rtf_border() object."
notes: the message names `border`, not the zone argument that was wrong

statement: style_zone(x = <a list of pages>) applies the same merge to every page, and an element that is not an rtftable stops as for the other verbs.

style_zone() warns once a session, "The edges of `rtf_border()` now mean the *outer* edges of whatever you attach it to.", when a zone border sets left/right (or a multi-row zone's top/bottom) without naming inside_v / inside_h, since its reading changed at 0.5.0.
style_zone() with an argument it does not have (headr = ) warns "`style_zone()`: unknown argument `headr` (did you mean `header`?) ignored." and ignores it.

rtf_table_style() returns a list of class rtf_table_style; rtftable() copies the fields it needs at construction (a snapshot), so changing or deriving a style afterwards does not change tables already built.

rtf_table_style(border_header, border_spanning, border_body, border_first_row, border_last_row = ) are the rtf_border() of the column-header rows, spanning rows, data rows, first and last data row; NULL (the default) is no border for the zone.
rtf_table_style(border_header = ) (likewise the other four) that is not NULL or an rtf_border() stops: "`border_header` must be NULL or an rtf_border object."
rtf_table_style(header_align = NULL) (the default) lets the header labels inherit the data alignment; "left", "center" or "right" sets it.
rtf_table_style(header_bold = FALSE, header_italic = FALSE) are the default look of the column-header labels; any value other than TRUE is stored as FALSE.
rtf_table_style(align = NULL) (the default) leaves each column's own default alignment (row-title columns left, the others centred); "left", "center" or "right" sets every column.
rtf_table_style(bold = FALSE, italic = FALSE, underline = FALSE) are the default look of the data cells; any value other than TRUE is stored as FALSE.
rtf_table_style(cell_padding_left_twips = , cell_padding_right_twips = ) are the cell padding of header and data cells, in twips; NULL (the default) leaves the document's padding.
rtf_table_style(row_height_twips = ) is the row height in twips; NULL (the default) is the font-aware default.
print() of an rtf_table_style lists the five zones (the border as <rtf_border> or none), header_align (or "(inherit align)"), header_bold, align (or "(per column)"), bold and the cell padding.
A style passed as rtftable(border = <style>), or as rtftable(style = ) while border is left at its default, gives the table the style's five border zones.

rtf_table_style_tfl() returns an rtf_table_style whose border_header is a top and a bottom rule (single, 15 twips, black), all other zones NULL, header_bold FALSE and header_align NULL (inherit the data alignment); each call builds a new object.
A table built with rtf_table_style_tfl() has rules on the column-header block only (top on the topmost header row, bottom on the bottommost), no vertical lines and no borders on the data section.

A multi-column spanning cell in a table with the TFL style gets an extra bottom rule (the group underline) only where the next header row subdivides the columns it covers, not where the span repeats unchanged.
rtf_table_style_tfl() takes no argument; to change a field, derive from it with rtf_table_style_with().
rtf_table_style_with(style, ...) returns a new rtf_table_style with the named fields replaced; the original is not changed.
rtf_table_style_with(style = ) is the rtf_table_style to derive from; (...) are named replacements for the fields rtf_table_style() has as arguments.
rtf_table_style_with() on something that is not an rtf_table_style stops: "`style` must be an rtf_table_style object."
rtf_table_style_with() with a field name the style does not have stops: "Unknown style field: 'nonexistent'"

rtf_table_border() warns once a session, "`rtf_table_border()` is deprecated: a border is now written once with `rtf_border()`, and *where* it applies is decided by where you attach it. ...", and still returns the same value as the internal constructor: a list of class rtf_table_border.

rtf_table_border(header, spanning, body, first_row, last_row = ) are the rtf_border() of the column-header rows, spanning rows, data rows, the first and the last data row; NULL (the default) is none, and first_row and last_row are overrides merged on top of body.
rtf_table_border(header = ) (likewise spanning, body, first_row, last_row) that is not NULL or an rtf_border() stops: "`header` must be NULL or an rtf_border object."
rtf_table_border(outer = ) is an rtf_border() whose four edges are the table's outermost edges; NULL (the default) is none.
rtf_table_border(outer = ) that is not NULL or an rtf_border() stops: "`outer` must be NULL or an rtf_border object (the table's four outermost edges)."
rtf_table_border(inside_h = , inside_v = ) are rtf_border_line() sides for the rules between rows and between cells; NULL (the default) is no rule.
rtf_table_border(inside_h = ) that is not NULL or an rtf_border_line() stops: "`inside_h` must be NULL or an rtf_border_line object."

Before drawing, outer, inside_h and inside_v are expanded into the zones: outer top to the topmost row (the header, else the first data row), outer bottom to the last data row, outer left and right and inside_v to the cell edges of the header and body zones, inside_h to every boundary between rows including the header/body seam.
print() of an rtf_table_border lists each zone as T / B / L / R sides (or none), and the outer, inside_h and inside_v lines when set.

rtf_border() returns a list of class rtf_border with the six slots top, bottom, left, right, inside_h, inside_v; it says everything about the border it returns, every side not named being unset (NULL), and building one never changes another.
notes: the help says to derive a border from another by passing it as `from`, and that TRUE is a rule in "this call's style / width / color"; rtf_border() has no from, style, width or color argument, TRUE being an rtf_border_line() with the defaults (single, 15 twips, black)

statement: rtf_border(top, bottom, left, right = ) are the selection's outer edges; each takes TRUE (a rule in single style, 15 twips, black), FALSE or "none" (an explicit no-line), a style name ("single", "double", "thick", "dash", "dot"), an rtf_border_line(), or NULL (unset).
rtf_border(all = ) is shorthand for top, bottom, left and right at once; a side named explicitly wins over it. rtf_border(all = FALSE) erases (no rule anywhere) while rtf_border() says nothing.

rtf_border(inside_h = , inside_v = ) are the rules between the selection's rows and between its cells, with the same values as the edges; NULL (the default) means no rule there, and they are not printed when unset.

rtf_border(top = "not-a-side") stops: "`top` must be one of "single", "double", "thick", "dash", "dot", "none", not "not-a-side"."; a value of another kind (a list, a number) stops: "`top` must be TRUE, FALSE, a border style name, an rtf_border_line(), or NULL."; the message names the slot, inside_h and inside_v included.
TRUE and "single" agree, FALSE and "none" are interchangeable, so rtf_border(top = TRUE, bottom = FALSE) is identical to rtf_border(top = "single", bottom = "none").

A side is in one of three states, unset (NULL, inherits what the enclosing selection supplies), erased (FALSE / "none", overrides an inherited rule) or a rule; adding to a border already in place is done where it is attached (style_zone(), style_header(), style_body()), which merge side by side.

An rtf_border records, as an attribute not part of its value, which of inside_h and inside_v the caller named, so that a border written for the pre-0.5.0 reading of left / right can be told apart and warned about (once a session).
A border line saved under the old class name rtf_border_side is still accepted as a side.
print() of an rtf_border lists top, bottom, left and right (none when unset) with style, width and colour, and inside_h and inside_v only when set.
rtf_border_bottom(style, width, color) returns rtf_border(bottom = rtf_border_line(style, width, color)): a border with the bottom edge only, defaults "single", 15L and NULL.
rtf_border_bottom() warns once a session, "`rtf_border_bottom()` is deprecated: write `rtf_border(bottom = TRUE)` instead.  See ?rtf_border.", and still returns its value.
rtf_border_bottom() with a style, width or colour rtf_border_line() refuses stops with that function's message.
rtf_border_box(style, width, color) returns rtf_border(all = rtf_border_line(style, width, color)): a border with all four outer edges alike, defaults "single", 15L and NULL.
rtf_border_box() warns once a session, "`rtf_border_box()` is deprecated: write `rtf_border(all = TRUE)` instead.  See ?rtf_border.", and still returns its value.
rtf_border_box() with a style, width or colour rtf_border_line() refuses stops with that function's message.
rtf_border_line() returns a list of class rtf_border_line holding style, width and color, the value a border side holds; the three can differ from side to side in one rtf_border().

rtf_border_line(style = "single") is one of "single", "double", "thick", "dash", "dot" or "none"; "none" is an explicit no-line which overrides an inherited border when merged on top of another, unlike NULL.
rtf_border_line(style = ) outside those values is refused by match.arg() ("'arg' should be one of ...").
rtf_border_line(width = 15L) is the line weight in twips (about 0.5 pt), converted to integer; it is ignored when style = "none".
rtf_border_line(width = ) below 1 with a style other than "none" stops: "`width` must be a positive integer (twips)."
rtf_border_line(color = NULL) (the default) is black; otherwise a 6-digit hex string such as "#003366".
rtf_border_line(color = ) that is not NULL or one "#RRGGBB" string stops: "`color` must be NULL or a 6-digit hex color string (e.g. \"#FF0000\")."
print() of an rtf_border_line shows "<rtf_border_line: double, 20 twips, color=#FF0000>", the colour only when set.
rtf_border_none() returns rtf_border(), a border with no side set.
rtf_border_none() warns once a session, "`rtf_border_none()` is deprecated: write `rtf_border()` instead.  See ?rtf_border.", and still returns its value.
rtf_border_side(style, width, color) returns exactly what rtf_border_line() with the same arguments returns, and its guards are rtf_border_line()'s.
rtf_border_side() warns once a session, "`rtf_border_side()` is deprecated: it is `rtf_border_line()` now (the same arguments).  The old name is removed in 0.9.0."
An object of the old class rtf_border_side, saved before the rename, is still read as a side by rtf_border() without a warning.

rtf_border_tfl(style, width, color) returns an rtf_table_border whose header has the line as top and bottom rule and whose spanning, body, first_row and last_row are NULL; defaults "single", 15L and NULL.

rtf_border_tfl() warns once a session, "`rtf_border_tfl()` is deprecated: the clinical TFL rules are already reachable as `rtftable(border = \"tfl\")`, and as a reusable value from `rtf_table_style_tfl()`.", and still returns its value.

A table with the TFL border has rules on the column-header block only, no vertical lines and none on the data; a multi-column spanning cell gets a group underline only where the columns below it are subdivided.
rtf_border_tfl() with a style, width or colour rtf_border_line() refuses stops with that function's message.
rtf_border_top(style, width, color) returns rtf_border(top = rtf_border_line(style, width, color)): a border with the top edge only, defaults "single", 15L and NULL.
rtf_border_top() warns once a session, "`rtf_border_top()` is deprecated: write `rtf_border(top = TRUE)` instead.  See ?rtf_border.", and still returns its value.
rtf_border_top() with a style, width or colour rtf_border_line() refuses stops with that function's message.
rtf_border_with(border, ...) returns a new rtf_border with the sides given replaced on top of border; sides not given (or NULL) are unchanged and the original is not changed.
rtf_border_with(border = ) is an rtf_border; NULL is treated as an empty border.
rtf_border_with(border = ) that is neither NULL nor an rtf_border stops: "`border` must be NULL or an rtf_border object."

rtf_border_with(top, bottom, left, right, inside_h, inside_v = ) are the replacement sides, in the values rtf_border() takes (TRUE, FALSE, a style name, an rtf_border_line()); "none" or FALSE erases a side.
rtf_border_with() warns once a session, "`rtf_border_with()` is deprecated. Layering happens where a border is attached: ...", and still returns its value.

cell_rows(...) returns an object of class cell_rows, a named list with one element per argument, for the cells argument of widen_ard() and plan_cells(); it is the shape a named row whose value is itself a chain, which c() would flatten, needs.
cell_rows(...) takes one argument per output row; its name is the row label, and an unnamed argument takes its label from `label`, as a bare template does.

cell_rows(<name> = ) holds a template ("{n:.0f}"), a chain of templates tried in order, or a chain with guards (n == 0 ~ "0", then "{n:.0f} ({estimate:.1f%})"); a single bare guard is a row too (#549).
cell_rows() with no argument stops: "`cell_rows()` needs at least one row."
print() of a cell_rows object prints "<cell_rows> n row(s)" and one line per row, its label (or "(from `label`)") and its chain with the guards written out.
In widen_ard(cells = ) and plan_cells() a cell_rows() puts each line on the variable's row of that label ("1" the first), so a statistic on one row only is expressed as a named row.

col_cell(pos, label, ...) returns a list of class rtf_col_cell holding pos and label, and align, bold, italic, underline and border only when given; positions are always those of the underlying data columns, not of the header row above.
col_cell(pos = <number>) is one column; c(start, end) is an inclusive range of columns, start <= end, values at least 1.

col_cell(pos = ) that is NA, of a length other than 1 or 2, or not a number, a string or a function stops: "`pos` must be a number or a column name of length 1 or 2, or a selector function such as col_key()."; a value below 1 stops "`pos` values must be >= 1."; a range with start > end stops "`pos` start must be <= end."

col_cell(pos = <column name>) names one column, or c(from, to) a range of columns by name, resolved against the data columns when the header is attached to a table, which keeps a spanning cell right when columns are reordered.

col_cell(pos = "") (an empty column name) stops: "`pos` column names must be non-empty strings."; when the header is attached, an unknown name stops: "`pos` column name \"zzz\" not found in data columns. Available: \"a\", \"b\"." and a name matching two columns, "`pos` column name \"x\" is ambiguous (matches 2 columns)."

col_cell(pos = <function>) is a selector of the data column names (see col_key()) returning a logical, integer or character vector; the matched columns must be adjacent and it is resolved when the header is attached.
col_cell(label = "") is the cell text (a scalar, may be empty; NULL is ""; only the first element of a longer vector is used).
col_cell(align = NULL) (the default) inherits the leftmost covered column's header_align; "left", "center" or "right" sets the cell.
col_cell(align = ) other than NULL, "left", "center", "right" stops: "`align` must be NULL, \"left\", \"center\", or \"right\"."
col_cell(bold = FALSE, italic = FALSE, underline = FALSE) set the flag on the cell; only TRUE is recorded.

col_cell(border = NULL) (the default) inherits the zone borders; an rtf_border() applies to this header cell only and overrides the zone border and the automatic group underline, e.g. border = rtf_border(bottom = "none") removes the underline under one spanning cell.
col_cell(border = ) that is not NULL or an rtf_border() stops: "`border` must be NULL or an rtf_border object."
print() of an rtf_col_cell shows "<col_cell pos=2..5 label=\"Treatment\" ...>" with the alignment and the b / i / u flags, and the selector's label for a function pos.
col_key(key) returns a function of the column names, tagged for use as col_cell(pos = ), that is TRUE for the columns whose name segment is one of key; the columns without the separator never match.
col_key(key = ) is one or more segment values to match (as.character); several keys select the columns of any of them.
col_key(key = ) that is empty, NA or holds an empty string stops: "`key` must be one or more non-empty strings."
col_key(sep = NULL) (the default) auto-detects the separator that occurs in the column names, "____" first and then tfrmt's delimiter; a single string uses that separator.
notes: help says the separator is the one of as_rtftables(header_sep = ) so that they stay in step, but col_key() detects only "____" and tfrmt's delimiter and is not told a custom header_sep, so sep must then be given

statement: col_key(sep = ) that is not NULL or one non-empty string stops: "`sep` must be NULL or a single non-empty string."
col_key(part = 1L) is the segment to compare, counted from the left (1 is the value before the first separator); a negative value counts from the right (-1 the last segment).
col_key(part = 0) stops: "`part` must be a non-zero integer."; a name with too few segments gives NA and does not match.

A col_key() selector that matches no column stops when the header is attached, "col_key("Plcebo") matched no data columns. Available keys: ...", listing the keys; one matching columns that are not adjacent stops "... matched non-adjacent data columns (2, 4, 6); a header cell can only span a contiguous range."

A selector must be handed the data column names: attached without them it stops "A selector `pos` in col_cell() requires the header to be attached to a table (data column names are unknown here)."; one returning something else than a logical of the right length, positions in range, existing names or a vector stops with a message naming the selector.

rtftable(blank_rows = ) given explicitly wins over the positions set_blank_rows() stored on the data frame (attr "rtf_blank_rows"); with blank_rows left NULL and read_attributes = TRUE (the default) the attribute is used, and with read_attributes = FALSE it is ignored.

blank_rows given as a list of positions, "between_groups", blank_rows_by_change() and blank_rows_by_rule() puts a blank wherever any of them says so, once: the positions of every entry are unioned and duplicates dropped; blank_row_first and blank_row_end add 0 and nrow(data) to the same set.

set_blank_rows(group_col = , group_by = ) change the meaning of blank_rows = "between_groups" only: a blank_rows_by_change() carries its own cols and group_by, a blank_rows_by_rule() its own col, and integer positions use neither.

set_decimal_split() on a column that also has style_cols() / style_body() settings: per-cell styles (alignment, border, fill, font) follow the column onto both halves; a per-cell align override cannot break the pair (the halves stay right and left); the interior vertical rule and the padding between the halves are suppressed.

style_body(border = ) is merged per side on top of the border the row's zone gives (body crossed with first_row and last_row): a side it names wins, one it leaves NULL keeps the zone's, "none" erases the zone's rule on the selected cells only; repeated calls layer per side.

style_header(border = ), style_zone() and style_cols(border = ) merge per side, last writer wins: a second call adds to the first (the first call's top survives a second call's bottom), a later call can change or erase (FALSE) a side, and a side left NULL says nothing.

style_header() on a character label row changes where the setting lives: bold, italic and align go to the columns' header styling shared by all label rows, while a border or underline request promotes the row to cells first; the rendered output of the promotion alone is unchanged.

style_body(background = ) overrides the column's fill given by style_cols(background = ) on the selected cells, and style_cols(header_background = ) fills only the header, so a shaded header does not shade the body.

A style passed as rtftable(style = ) provides defaults only: an explicit col_header_align, row_height_twips, cell_padding_left_twips or cell_padding_right_twips always wins over the style's field, and the style's borders are adopted only while border is left at its default "tfl".

Resolution of a look field of rtf_table_style: an explicit rtftable() argument beats a col_spec entry, which beats the style's field, which beats the package default; a style that does not say align leaves each column's own default (row-title left, others centred).

rtf_table_border(outer = , inside_h = , inside_v = ), the whole-table shortcuts, are expanded into the five zones first, and a zone given explicitly is merged on top and wins ("whole table, except ...").

The same rtf_border() means the selection it is attached to: the whole table at rtftable(border = ) (edges the outer frame, inside_h / inside_v the rules between rows and cells), one kind of row at style_zone(), one cell at col_cell(border = ) where there is no inside; an edge is always the selection's outer edge.
On a header row with a spanning cell, rtf_border(inside_v = ) lands on cell boundaries, not column boundaries, because nothing is drawn inside a merged cell.
rtf_border(all = , top = ): a side named explicitly wins over all, whichever order they are written in.

col_cell(border = ) on a header cell overrides the zone border and the automatic group underline for that cell only: border = rtf_border(bottom = "none") removes one underline and leaves every other rule.

col_cell(pos = <selector function or column name>) is resolved against the final data column names when the header is attached, so it is not shifted when a stub column is prepended or columns are remapped, unlike a numeric pos; paginate_cols() refuses to cut inside a selector span.
A listing: records laid out in columns, each column's variables stacked or joined, wrapped to a width, repeats collapsed, the widths fitted to the page.

build_listing() turns source data (a data.frame, one row per record) and a listing_spec() into the data.frame a listing prints: source variables joined into printed columns, long cells broken over as many physical rows as they need, gutter columns between the printed ones, a blank row after each record and a hidden record column; the result carries the spec for as_rtftables().

listing_spec() bundles the printed columns of a listing and the settings that apply to all of them into one rtf_listing_spec object that build_listing() and as_rtftables(listing = ) both read; type names a template that supplies every default, and any argument given overrides it.

listing_col() describes one printed column of a listing: the source variables it is built from, how they are joined, how wide it may be before its text wraps onto a further physical row, and its header; it returns an rtf_listing_col object.
listing_take() cuts a string to the longest prefix whose display width fits a given width, never "" for non-empty text.

listing_wrap() breaks a listing cell or header into the lines it occupies, by the "multiline" type's own rule: after the separator, then at a word boundary, then a hard split, every line fitting the width.
listing_wrap_code() writes the default wrapping rule (the policy functions of listing_wrap()) out as source, ready to paste into a script and edit, and to pass as listing_spec(wrap = ).

listing_code() writes a listing_spec() out as the code that would build it (class rtf_listing_code), only what differs from the listing's defaults, so a spec from fit_listing_widths() can be pasted into a program and tuned.
listing_disp_width() measures the display width of text, where a full-width (CJK) glyph counts as two columns, vectorised over its input.
listing_split_after() breaks one string after each separator and keeps the separator at the end of the piece it closes.

fit_listing_widths() fills in the width of every listing_col() that does not set one, by measuring what each column demands and fitting the demands into the character budget the page leaves, and returns the same listing_spec() with the measurement attached.

collapse_repeats() blanks consecutive repeated values in chosen columns of a finished rtftable, or of each page of a list of them, keeping the first row of each run; suppressed cells become NA and no row is removed.
catx() joins values element by element with a separator, leaving out every value that is missing or empty, as SAS CATX does; it is the join listing_col() applies to its vars.

build_listing(data, spec) returns a data.frame of the printed columns in order with the gutter columns between them and, unless record = FALSE, the hidden record column last; it carries the spec as the attribute rtf_listing.
build_listing() joins each printed column's vars with the column's separator, skipping missing and empty values, so a record missing its middle value prints no doubled separator.

build_listing() breaks a cell longer than its column's width over as many physical rows as it needs, and pads every column of one record to the tallest so the record's rows stay aligned across columns.

build_listing() ends each record's block with a blank row when the spec has blank_row = TRUE, and the hidden record column holds the source row number on every physical row of the record, its blank row included.
build_listing() puts a gutter column (named .sp1, .sp2, ...) between each pair of printed columns when the spec has spacer = TRUE, and none when spacer = FALSE; the gutters are blank on every row.
build_listing() appends the record column under the name the spec gives it (.rtf_record by default, a name given to record =), and appends none when record = FALSE.

build_listing() resolves a column's omitted label against the data (each source column's label attribute, else its name) and hands the resolved spec back on the body, so as_rtftables() and a second build never derive it again.
A factor source column is joined by its labels, not its level codes.
build_listing() on a data frame of zero rows returns a data frame of zero rows with the same column names as for data (gutter and record columns included), not an error.
build_listing(data, spec) |> as_rtftables() renders the same listing as as_rtftables(data, listing = spec): the body carries its spec, the record column decides the page breaks and is not printed.

build_listing(data = <an rlistings listing_df>) stops: "`data` is an rlistings listing (`listing_df`), which rlistings has already laid out -- its display columns, key-column suppression and titles are baked in.  Pass it straight to `as_rtftables()` instead of building a listing from it."
build_listing(data = 1:3) (anything not a data.frame or tibble) stops: "`data` must be a data.frame or tibble; got '<class>'."
build_listing(spec = "spec") (anything not from listing_spec()) stops: "`spec` must be a listing_spec(); got '<class>'."
build_listing() on data that is already a build_listing() body stops: "`data` has already been through build_listing() -- building it again would join columns that are already joined."
build_listing() with a listing_col() whose vars are not all in data stops, naming them: `Column "NOPE" not in `data` (listing column "NOPE").` (`Columns "A", "B" not in ...` for several).

build_listing() with a record column named like a printed column (listing_spec(record = "USUBJID") over a column USUBJID) stops: "The record column "USUBJID" collides with a printed column of the same name; rename one."

build_listing() with a custom wrap that returns anything but a non-empty character vector stops, for a cell and for a header alike: "The listing's `wrap` function must return a non-empty character vector of lines."
listing_spec(cols) returns an object of class rtf_listing_spec holding the columns and every setting resolved against the type's template; printing it shows the columns and settings it will use.

listing_spec(cols = ) takes the printed columns in order as a list of listing_col() objects; a bare string or character vector stands for listing_col() on each element, and a single listing_col() object is one column.
listing_spec() gives two columns that would get the same output name distinct names: the later ones get the suffix _1, _2, ... (A, A_1).

listing_spec(type = "multiline") (the default) supplies every default below: sep "/", spacer TRUE, spacer_rel_width 1, blank_row TRUE, blank_row_first TRUE, align "left", layout "stack", and the separator-then-word wrapping rule.
listing_spec(sep = " | ") sets the separator for every listing_col() that does not set its own; NULL (the default) takes the template's "/".
listing_spec(spacer = FALSE) leaves out the narrow blank gutter column between each pair of printed columns; NULL (the default) takes the template's TRUE.
listing_spec(spacer_rel_width = 0.25) sets the relative width of the gutter columns, a fraction allowed; NULL (the default) takes the template's 1.
listing_spec(blank_row = FALSE) ends no record's block with a blank row; NULL (the default) takes the template's TRUE.

listing_spec(blank_row_first = FALSE) does not start each page with a blank row; the setting is passed on as as_rtftables(blank_row_first = ), which makes it per page rather than once per listing; NULL (the default) takes the template's TRUE.
listing_spec(align = "center") is the default alignment of every column that sets none; "left", "center" or "right"; NULL (the default) takes the template's "left".

listing_spec(layout = "flow") is the default cell layout of every column that sets none: "stack" breaks after every separator, "flow" fills each line as far as the width allows; NULL (the default) takes the template's "stack".

listing_spec(wrap = f) replaces the type's wrapping rule with a function(text, width, sep, layout) that lays out the cells and the derived headers alike; NULL (the default) uses the type's own rule, and wrap = listing_wrap changes nothing.

A custom wrap is called positionally with four arguments: text (a length-1 character), width (a positive number or NULL for a column with none), sep (the effective separator) and layout ("stack" or "flow", already resolved), and returns a non-empty character vector, one element per line.

listing_spec(record = TRUE) (the default) appends the hidden record column under its standard name .rtf_record, record = FALSE appends none, and a single string names it; as_rtftables(listing = ) splits with "group_safe" on it and does not print it.
listing_spec() takes no labels argument: the words for source variables belong to fit_listing_widths(labels = ).
listing_spec() with no cols (missing or NULL) stops: "`cols` is required: the printed columns, in order."
listing_spec(cols = list()) (or anything that is not a non-empty list) stops: "`cols` must be a non-empty list of listing_col() objects (or column names)."
listing_spec(cols = list(1L)) stops, naming the element: "`cols[[1]]` must be a listing_col() or a character vector of source column names; got 'integer'."

listing_spec(type = "nope") stops: "Unknown listing type "nope".  Available: "multiline"."; a type that is not a single non-empty string stops: "`type` must be a single listing-template name; see ?listing_spec."
listing_spec(spacer = "yes") stops: "`spacer` must be TRUE or FALSE, or NULL."; the same text for blank_row and blank_row_first with their own names.
listing_spec(spacer_rel_width = 0) (not a single positive number) stops: "`spacer_rel_width` must be a single positive number, or NULL."
listing_spec(align = "middle") or layout = "sideways" stops with match.arg()'s "'arg' should be one of ..." message.

listing_spec(wrap = "not a function") stops: "`wrap` must be a function(text, width, sep, layout) returning the lines, or NULL for the type's own rule."; a function with fewer than four arguments stops: "`wrap` must accept four arguments: text, width, sep, layout."
listing_spec(record = 3) stops: "`record` must be TRUE, FALSE, or a single column name."

listing_col("USUBJID") returns an rtf_listing_col with the output name the first of vars, no width (never wraps), no label (derived from the data), and the listing's own sep, align and layout; printing it shows what it will do.
listing_col(vars = c("AEDECOD", "AELOC")) joins one or more source columns in the order given, with sep, skipping missing and empty values.
listing_col(sep = " / ") is the separator between this column's vars; NULL (the default) takes the listing's own ("/" under the "multiline" type).

listing_col(width = 15) is the maximum display width in characters per physical row before the cell wraps (a full-width glyph counts as two), kept as an integer; NULL (the default) never wraps this column. It does not set the column's width in the table (rel_width does).
listing_col(label = c("Unique", "Subject ID")): a character vector is the header's lines, one element one line, laid out already and not re-wrapped.
listing_col(label = "Unique\nSubject ID"): a string carrying its own line breaks is a layout too and is used exactly as written.

listing_col(label = "Preferred term of the event", width = 16): a single string with no breaks is words for the package to lay out, wrapped to width by the cells' rule, or left as one line when there is no width.

listing_col(label = NULL) (the default) derives the header from the data: each source column's label attribute when it has one, otherwise its name, joined with sep and wrapped to the width as the cells are, or from fit_listing_widths(labels = ).
A derived header follows its column: stacked, it breaks at the separator as the cell does; flowed, a cell on one line gets a header on one line (two labels can share a line).
listing_col(label = "") asks for a deliberately empty header.
listing_col(name = "COL01") is the output column name; NULL (the default) uses the first entry of vars.
listing_col(rel_width = 12) is the column's relative width in the rendered table; NULL (the default) uses width when there is one, otherwise the longest line of label, otherwise 10.
notes: The help text omits the final fallback of 10 when there is neither width nor label.

statement: listing_col(align = "right") is the column's alignment ("left", "center" or "right"); NULL (the default) takes the listing's own ("left" under "multiline").

listing_col(layout = "flow") fills each line as far as width allows, treating the separator as a break opportunity, so short parts (an age and a sex) share a row; "stack" breaks after every separator so each source column starts its own line; NULL (the default) takes the listing's own ("stack"). With no width both behave alike.

listing_col(collapse_repeats = TRUE) marks a key column: its single-line value is carried down every physical row of its record, the record's blank row included, so as_rtftables() blanks the repeats per page and the value prints once per run of records that share it, and reappears at the top of the next page.
A key column whose cell already wraps onto several lines is padded as usual and not carried down, because there is no one value to repeat; an unmarked column is always padded with blanks.
listing_col() with no vars, NULL, a non-character, an empty vector, an NA or an empty string stops: "`vars` must be one or more non-empty source column names."
listing_col(sep = c(",", ";")) (not a single string or NULL) stops: "`sep` must be a single string, or NULL."
listing_col(width = 0) (not a single number of at least 1, or NULL) stops: "`width` must be a single positive number of characters, or NULL."
listing_col(rel_width = -1) stops: "`rel_width` must be a single positive number, or NULL."
listing_col(label = 1:2), character(0) or a vector with an NA stops: "`label` must be a string, or a character vector of header lines, or NULL."
listing_col(name = "") or a vector of two stops: "`name` must be a single non-empty string, or NULL."
listing_col(align = "middle") or layout = "sideways" stops with match.arg()'s "'arg' should be one of ..." message.
listing_col(collapse_repeats = NA) (or "yes") stops: "`collapse_repeats` must be TRUE or FALSE."
listing_take(x, width) returns the longest prefix of the string x whose display width is at most width, so listing_take("HYPERGLYCAEMIA", 6) is "HYPERG".
listing_take(x, width) counts a full-width (CJK) glyph as two columns, so a prefix never exceeds width in display.
listing_take() never returns "" for non-empty x, even where the first glyph is wider than width, so a caller looping on the remainder always makes progress.
listing_take("", width) returns "".
listing_wrap(text, width) returns, for a length-1 text, a character vector of lines: listing_wrap("COMPLETED/UPPER/HYPERGLYCAEMIA", 22) is c("COMPLETED/", "UPPER/", "HYPERGLYCAEMIA").
listing_wrap() is exactly the "multiline" type's own rule, so listing_spec(wrap = listing_wrap) changes nothing.

listing_wrap(text, width, sep = "/") breaks first after the separator, which stays at the end of the line it closes; sep = "" or NULL skips this step; a regex-special separator such as "." is taken literally.
listing_wrap() breaks a piece still wider than width at a word boundary (after a space, a comma or a hyphen), filling each line as far as width allows.
listing_wrap() hard-splits a token still too wide on its own, so every returned line fits width.
listing_wrap() measures width as display width: a full-width (CJK) glyph counts as two.
listing_wrap() honours a line break already in text before any other rule, and takes NA or "" as an empty cell returning "".

listing_wrap(layout = "stack") (the default) breaks after every separator; "flow" treats the separator as a break opportunity and fills the line, so listing_wrap("40/F", 20, layout = "flow") is "40/F".
listing_wrap(width = NULL) means no limit: text is returned as it stands (trimmed), whatever the layout.
listing_wrap() on a text vector of length more than one wraps element by element and returns a list of character vectors.
listing_wrap(sep = c("/", "-")) (not a single string or NULL) stops: "`sep` must be a single string, or NULL."
listing_wrap(width = -1) (not a single number of at least 1, or NULL) stops: "`width` must be a single positive number, or NULL."

listing_wrap_code(name) returns the policy of the default wrapping rule as source lines of class rtf_listing_code (printing writes the code out); evaluated, it defines the entry function name, name_flow and name_words, and name(text, width, sep, layout) gives the same lines as listing_wrap().
The emitted source needs no rtfreporter::: and no internal function: it calls the exported listing_disp_width(), listing_take() and listing_split_after() rather than carrying copies.
listing_wrap_code(name = "edited") (default "my_wrap") names the entry function, the one to pass as wrap; the helpers are prefixed with it, so two edited rules can live in one script.
The emitted source keeps the shipped rule's comments and begins with a header naming the package version, the entry function (wrap = name) and the wrap contract.
The emitted rule is regenerated from the shipped functions and must not drift from them.
listing_wrap_code(name = "") or a vector of two (not a single non-empty string) stops: "`name` must be a single non-empty string."
listing_wrap_code(name = "2fast") stops: "`name` must be a syntactic R name; got "2fast"."

listing_code(spec) returns a character vector, one element per line of code, of class rtf_listing_code whose printing shows the code ready to copy, and parsing it gives back the spec (the same widths and headers).
listing_code() writes out only what differs from the listing's defaults (the type's template), so the result reads like something a person wrote.

listing_code() writes each column's own settings: vars, width, sep, layout, name when it is not the first var, rel_width, align, collapse_repeats = TRUE, and a multi-line label (kept through the round trip).
listing_code() on a spec fitted by fit_listing_widths() writes width, rel_width and label on every column.
listing_code(name = "listing") writes listing <- listing_spec(...); NULL (the default) writes the call alone.
listing_code(indent = 4) sets the number of spaces the listing_col() calls are indented by; the default is 2.
listing_code() on a spec with a custom wrap function writes a comment saying it cannot be written out and that wrap = must be added back when pasted.
listing_code(spec = "spec") (not a listing_spec()) stops: "`spec` must be a listing_spec(); got 'character'."
listing_code(name = "") (not a single non-empty string or NULL) stops: "`name` must be a single non-empty string, or NULL."
listing_code(indent = -1) (not a single non-negative integer) stops: "`indent` must be a single non-negative integer."

listing_disp_width(x) returns an integer vector of the display widths of x, counting a full-width (CJK) glyph as two columns, so listing_disp_width(c("ABC", <three full-width characters>)) is c(3L, 6L).
listing_disp_width() takes NA as the empty string (width 0) and non-character input by its text (42 is 2L, a factor by its label).
listing_disp_width(character(0)) returns integer(0); the function is vectorised over x.
listing_split_after(text, sep) breaks text after each separator and keeps the separator at the end of the piece it closes: listing_split_after("COMPLETED/UPPER", "/") is c("COMPLETED/", "UPPER").
listing_split_after() takes sep literally, not as a regular expression: listing_split_after("a.b", ".") is c("a.", "b").
listing_split_after(text, sep = "") or sep = NULL returns text unsplit.

fit_listing_widths(data, spec) returns the same listing_spec() with a width on every column, and attaches the measurement (rtf_listing_fit: total width, gutter, each column's demand, which columns were fixed), which print() shows.
fit_listing_widths() makes the fitted widths and the gutters add up to the character budget exactly.
fit_listing_widths() takes the gutter columns out of the budget first (spacer_rel_width characters each, a fraction allowed), and none when the spec has spacer = FALSE.

fit_listing_widths() keeps every width the author set (a decision, not a proposal), takes it out of the budget, and fits the other columns around it; a spec whose widths are all set comes back with them unchanged.

A column's demand is the largest of the probs quantile of its cell display widths, the width its header needs to be no taller than header_lines, the widest token its header cannot break, and min_width; the demands are then scaled to the budget.
Scaling never takes a fitted column below the widest token its header cannot break, so a header is never cut mid-word; the characters are taken from columns with room to spare.

fit_listing_widths() writes the estimate down: alongside the fitted width each column gets rel_width and label (the label frozen unwrapped, with only its structural breaks), only where the author has not set them, and the result renders to the same table.

fit_listing_widths(page = rtf_page(...)) takes the paper size, orientation and margins the listing will be rendered on (an rtf_page() or a list of its fields) to compute the character budget; NULL (the default) uses the package's page defaults; ignored when total_width is given.
fit_listing_widths(font = ) is the font the listing renders in, used to turn the page width into a number of characters; NULL (the default) is getOption("rtfreporter.font").
